beats.text: A producer faster than its consumer...
beats.say: What happens when a producer sends data faster than a consumer can handle?

beats.text: The buffer fills: crash or drop data.
beats.say: The buffer in between fills up. Then you either run out of memory and crash, or start dropping data.

beats.text: Back pressure: the consumer says slow down.
beats.say: Back pressure is the consumer telling the producer: slow down.

beats.text: Slow the producer. Bound the buffer. Drop on purpose.
beats.say: There are three common responses: slow the producer down, keep the buffer bounded, or drop the least important data on purpose.

beats.text: Pull: ask for more only when ready.
beats.say: Many systems use pull instead of push. The consumer asks for the next batch only when it is ready, so overload is impossible by design.
Kafka consumers pull at their own pace, Reactive Streams build request n into the contract, and TCP uses a window size.
